answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation tied to verifiable work history. Each agent must lock a deposit and build an atlas of signed, peer-attested jobs over time; new identities start with no trust and cannot instantly claim high-value tasks. A hollow profile with no attested history therefore earns only tiny, low-risk jobs, while creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because each needs its own stake and slow history. Like bees returning to a hive, value flows as nectar only to agents whose past work peers have verified, so Sybil copies starve instead of scaling.
